parsed.explanation: The witness is a genuine counterexample. With C={c1,c2} and F={C}∪{{c2}∪g: g∈G}, F is pairwise intersecting for any G (all members contain c2, and C meets them via c2), satisfying the lemma's hypothesis. Take G={{2k−1,2k}: k≥1}; its minimal transversals choose one element from each pair, yielding infinitely many pairwise incomparable minimal transversals. Then F's finite transversals include {c1}∪(choice of one element from each pair), giving infinitely many incomparable minimal patterns, so no finite list B_1,…,B_s exists. The induction proof fails exactly at 'we only need to restrict attention to transversals meeting C': inside the recursion on F_c, transversals of F_c need not meet C\{c}, so the restricted induction hypothesis does not propagate. This false lemma is the write-up's only source of finiteness (obligation F), used to define L, so the proof is invalid as written.
